gap: No result ChatGPT got states that QNAP's route to 10GbE on its Intel 6-bays has a slot limit: the TS-664's only expansion slot is PCIe Gen 3 x2, which carries about 15.8 Gb/s, so one of the dual-port 10GbE cards QNAP lists for it (QXG-10G2T) cannot run both ports at full speed. QNAP also says to fit only QNAP memory, up to 16 GB. The TVS-h674 has Gen 4 x16 and Gen 4 x4 slots that take a card up to 185 × 111 mm.
standout_why: I compared against these pages. ChatGPT cited the QNAP TVS-h674 hardware spec page, which gives the TVS-h674's slots but says nothing about the TS-664. Starry Hope (cited in one chat) covers UGREEN Plex running in Docker and the TerraMaster TOS 7 package gap, but it has no QNAP models and nothing about 10GbE cards. Our current page names the QXG-10G1T and the TS-664's Gen3 x2 slot but not the bandwidth limit or the 16 GB memory ceiling. One QNAP compare page that included the TS-664 was in ChatGPT's results but not cited, and it probably lists the slot. Every ChatGPT answer says only '10GbE requires an additional card' for QNAP. The TS-664 slot limit is new but small, so 1.
decides: It supports the existing pick. The DXP6800 Pro and the TerraMaster F6-424 Max and F6-425 Pro have two 10GbE ports built in. QNAP's Intel 6-bays need a QXG card on top of the box price. On the TS-664, a dual-port card shares a Gen3 x2 slot that is slower than two 10GbE links. The TVS-h674 takes the card without a bandwidth limit, but it costs about twice as much. The finding argues against recommending 'TS-664 + 10GbE card' as a budget route to dual 10GbE. A single-port QXG-10G1T fits within the slot.

findings.label: PCIe expansion slot
findings.value: 1 slot, PCIe Gen 3 x2; card up to 190 × 68.9 × 18.76 mm
findings.note: QNAP lists 5GbE and 10GbE as 'Optional via PCIe expansion card'. The bandwidth figure is my arithmetic: PCIe 3.0 is about 0.985 GB/s per lane, × 2 lanes ≈ 1.97 GB/s ≈ 15.8 Gb/s. That is below the 20 Gb/s of two 10GbE ports, so a dual-port card cannot run both ports at line rate here. A single-port card (10 Gb/s) fits.

findings.label: 10GbE cards QNAP lists as optional accessories
findings.value: QXG-10G1T, QXG-10G2T, QXG-10G2SF-NXE, QM2-2P10G1TB (QXG-10G2TB marked EOL)
findings.note: These come from the 'optional accessories' list on QNAP's spec page. QNAP does not state per-card bandwidth limits there.

findings.label: Memory
findings.value: 2 × SODIMM DDR4, max 16 GB (2 × 8 GB); 8 GB installed on TS-664-8G
findings.note: QNAP: 'Use only QNAP memory modules to maintain system performance and stability.' The 4G model needs 'a pair of identical DDR4 modules'.

findings.label: PCIe expansion slots
findings.value: Slot 1: PCIe Gen 4 x16; Slot 2: PCIe Gen 4 x4; card up to 185 × 111.15 × 18.76 mm
findings.note: Built-in networking is 2× 2.5GbE. 5GbE and 10GbE are 'Optional via PCIe expansion card'. QNAP: 'Wider cards can be installed if the next PCIe slot will not be used.' The accessory list includes QXG 10GbE and 25GbE cards and QM2-2P10G1TB, some marked EOL.

findings.label: CPU / iGPU and memory by variant
findings.value: i5-12400 6C/12T (32 GB) or i3-12100 4C/8T (16 GB); Intel UHD Graphics 730; 2 × SODIMM DDR4, max 64 GB
findings.note: QNAP says to use only QNAP memory modules. The M.2 slots are 2 × 2280 PCIe Gen 4 x4, 'Compatible with NVMe SSD PCIe Gen 3 and above', and M.2 SSDs are not hot-swappable.

findings.label: Plex hardware transcoding (QNAP's own list)

findings.note: QNAP's recommended-NAS table names the TS-453E, TS-664 and TVS-h874T. It does not name the TVS-h674. QNAP: 'A Plex Pass account is required for hardware-accelerated streaming.' The page gives no QTS or QuTS hero version requirement.
